newsitem.title: USA: Clinton vulnerable to attack on character.
newsitem.headline: Clinton vulnerable to attack on character.

text.p: President Bill Clinton, heading into the final presidential debate, remains vulnerable to attacks on his character, pollster Frank Newport, editor-in-chief of the Gallup Poll, said on Tuesday.

Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole, who remained 18 points behind Clinton in the latest Gallup poll, was expected to go on the offensive in Wednesday's debate with Clinton in San Diego, Newport told a Houston business group.
"It is now viewed as his last hope, so I think it is probable Bob Dole will turn up the steam," Newport said. "(But) there's no way around the fact that Clinton looks good for re-election."
In the latest CNN/USA Today/Gallup tracking poll, Clinton held a 54 to 36 percent lead over Bob Dole with 4 percent favouring Reform party candidate Ross Perot.

At a Kansas City rally earlier this week, Dole called the White House unethical and compared the administration's handling of confidential FBI files to the Watergate scandal that ousted President Richard Nixon from office.

Clinton also has refused to rule out presidential pardons for some of his former partners in the failed Whitewater investment in Arkansas, and came under attack by Republicans for his ties to a wealthy Indonesian businessman.

With three weeks left in the campaign, Americans polled by Gallup remained evenly divided over the basic issue of whether Clinton is honest, although 55 percent believe he is honest enough to be president, Newport said.

But with relatively few voters voicing concern about critical issues like the economy that have unseated incumbents in the past, Clinton appeared a probable winner in the November election, Newport said.
"The bottom line is, we think the American public is saying with this election, why change?" he said.
